name: Jezero Crater — Perseverance landing site
summary: Crater-floor lava flows (Máaz/Séítah) beside an ancient lake delta with clays and carbonates; Perseverance landing site.

coord.source: Zafrir et al. 2026, Icarus 460, 117296 (doi:10.1016/j.icarus.2026.117296): Perseverance landed at 18.44 N, 77.45 E
coord.note: Secondary citation; Octavia E. Butler Landing. Values below are from MEDA along the early rover traverse, not one fixed point.

terrain.display: 231 m (P99 − P1, 10 × 10 km window at ~200 m)
terrain.citation: Fergason, R.L., Hare, T.M., Mayer, D.P., et al. 2020, Mars 2020 Terrain Relative Navigation Flight Product Generation: Digital Terrain Model and Orthorectified Image Mosaics, 51st LPSC, abstract #2020 (ADS 2020LPI....51.2020F)
terrain.note: USGS Mars 2020 TRN CTX DTM mosaic (JEZ_ctx_B_soc_008, 20 m, MOLA-areoid heights); native 20.0 m posting, native-resolution relief 233.3 m; products span 229–252 m. Cross-checks: HRSC-MOLA Blended DEM Global 200 m v2 [Fergason, R.L., Hare, T.M., & Laura, J. 2018, HRSC and MOLA Blended Digital Elevation Model at 200m v2, Astrogeology PDS Annex, USGS; https://planetarymaps.usgs.gov/mosaic/Mars/HRSC_MOLA_Blend/Mars_HRSC_MOLA_BlendDEM_Global_200mp_v2.tif] at 200.0x189.7 m: relief 252.0 m, median -2562.0 m, 50x53 px | MOLA MEGDR 128 pix/deg (~463 m), megt44n000hb [Smith, D.E., et al. 2001, JGR 106(E10), 23689, doi:10.1029/2000JE001364 (MOLA); PDS MGS-M-MOLA-5-MEGDR-L3-V1.0; https://pds-geosciences.wustl.edu/mgs/mgs-m-mola-5-megdr-l3-v1/mgsl_300x/meg128/megt44n000hb.img] at native 463x439 m (cannot be refined to 200 m; excluded from min/max): relief 255.9 m, median -2560.0 m, 22x23 px, 46% of pixels contain >=1 MOLA shot (rest interpolated, per megc44n000hb). relief_m = mean over all ~200 m block offsets (offset range 229.1–232.8 m); relief_min_m/relief_max_m span offsets and products; CTX cached; window 500x527 px, ground pixel 20.00 m N-S x 18.97 m E-W (eqc lat_ts=0, R=3396190 m); ~200 m posting = block-mean to 200.0 x 208.7 m; valid 100.0%; heights relative to the MOLA areoid in all products; relief comes mostly from km-scale slopes (crater floor / delta front), so 20 m vs 200 m posting differs little; product-to-product differences (source data, interpolation) dominate

aridity.citation: NASA Science, Mars Facts: "the Martian atmosphere is too thin for liquid water to exist for long on the surface"
aridity.note: Physical constraint, not a measurement; the page does not discuss precipitation explicitly.

temp.display: ≈ −52 °C (midpoint of daily-mean surface temperature 210–232 K over one Mars year)
temp.citation: Munguira et al. 2024, JGR Planets 129, e2024JE008385 — One Martian Year of Near-Surface Temperatures at Jezero From MEDA (results, Fig. 4a)
temp.note: No annual mean is published; we use the midpoint of the published range (derived). Normalized value could lie anywhere from 0 to 0.20 across that range.

temp_range.citation: Munguira et al. 2023, JGR Planets 128, e2022JE007559 — Near Surface Atmospheric Temperatures at Jezero From MEDA (conclusions; table: 81 K at Ls 25°, 104 K at Ls 180°)
temp_range.note: Uses the lower end of the published range; every value in the range exceeds Earth's bound (35 °C) and clips to 1. Coverage Ls 13–203° only.

veg.citation: NASA Science, Mars Facts: "Scientists don't expect to find living things currently thriving on Mars."
veg.note: NDVI is not defined for Mars; treated as NDVI 0 (bare).

geology.display: Basaltic lava flows (Máaz formation) on the crater floor
geology.citation: Sun et al. 2023, JGR Planets 128, e2022JE007613 (§1, §2.2.2); Farley et al. 2022, Science 377, eabo2196
geology.note: Applies to the landing site. The delta (not the landing site) hosts Fe/Mg clays and carbonates; it would map to 'clay'.

ice.display: No near-surface ice expected at 18° N
ice.citation: Piqueux et al. 2019, GRL 46, 14290 — shallow ice consistent with latitudes as low as 35° N / 45° S
ice.note: Inference from the latitude limit; no Jezero-specific statement found.

name: Lunar South Pole — Shackleton–de Gerlache connecting ridge (Artemis)
summary: Sunlit ridge near Shackleton crater in the Artemis exploration zone; anorthositic highlands next to permanently shadowed cold traps that hold water ice.

coord.source: NASA ACD-50044 Rev A, Lunar Surface Data Book (2023), Fig. 7.3.1: point C1 (89.468° S, 222.6° E) on the Shackleton–de Gerlache connecting ridge
coord.note: 222.6° E converted to −137.4°. Point definitions (C1/C2) differ between papers.

terrain.display: 1107 m (P99 − P1, 10 × 10 km window at ~200 m)
terrain.citation: Smith, D.E., et al. 2010, Initial observations from the Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter (LOLA), GRL 37, L18204, doi:10.1029/2010GL043751; PDS LRO-L-LOLA-4-GDR-V1.0
terrain.note: LRO LOLA LDEM_875S_20M (20 m, south polar stereographic, product V2.0 2017-06-15); native 20.0 m posting, native-resolution relief 1130.0 m; products span 1093–1125 m. Cross-checks: LRO LOLA LDEM_875S_5M (5 m, same release) [Smith, D.E., et al. 2010, Initial observations from the Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter (LOLA), GRL 37, L18204, doi:10.1029/2010GL043751; PDS LRO-L-LOLA-4-GDR-V1.0; https://pds-geosciences.wustl.edu/lro/lro-l-lola-3-rdr-v1/lrolol_1xxx/data/lola_gdr/polar/img/ldem_875s_5m.img, byte-range rows 16544-18543, cached] at 200.0x200.0 m: relief 1105.3 m (native 5 m: 1129.5 m), median 1441.0 m; 5 m block-mean to 20 m minus 20 m product: mean 0.0 m, RMS 0.7 m. relief_m = mean over all ~200 m block offsets (offset range 1093.4–1125.0 m); relief_min_m/relief_max_m span offsets and products; LOLA 20 m cached/cached; target map x=-10919.5 m, y=-11874.8 m (checked against PROJ); scale factor k=1.000022, window +/-5000.1 m = rows 4136-4636, cols 2996-3496 (500x500 px), valid 100.0%; heights = DN x 0.5 m relative to the 1737.4 km sphere; window min/max 531/1959 m; orientation check PASSED: 4 km window at Shackleton centre (USGS Gazetteer 89.67 S 129.78 E) median -2755 m vs lon-mirrored point 814 m; LOLA grids are interpolated between laser tracks (GMT blockmedian/surface), so true resolution is coarser than the pixel size; the window spans ridge crest and the steep Shackleton / de Gerlache flank slopes (which side the low end is was not checked), so relief is not ridge-top roughness

aridity.citation: NASA Science, Moon Facts: "The Moon's weak atmosphere and its lack of liquid water cannot support life as we know it."

temp.display: ≈ 200 K (−73 °C) in summer, colder in winter
temp.citation: Williams et al. 2019, JGR Planets 124, 2505 — Seasonal Polar Temperatures on the Moon (Diviner; text on Fig. 10d, Connecting Ridge)
temp.note: No annual mean is published. Summer ≈200 K is an upper bound, so the annual mean is below Earth's coldest bound (−60 °C) and clips to 0 whatever its exact value.

temp_range.note: No published day–night range for the ridge; at the pole, season and shadowing dominate over a simple diurnal cycle.

veg.citation: NASA Science, Moon Facts (no liquid water, cannot support life as we know it)
veg.note: NDVI is not defined for the Moon; treated as NDVI 0 (bare).

geology.display: Anorthosite (feldspathic highlands; regolith and breccia at the surface)
geology.citation: Patterson et al. 2024, JGR Planets 129, e2023JE008275 — Lithologies and Chronologic Opportunities of Materials to Be Returned From the Artemis Exploration Zone
geology.note: Interpretation from orbital data; surface is impact-processed regolith, possibly with South Pole–Aitken ejecta.

ice.display: Water ice in nearby permanently shadowed regions
ice.citation: Colaprete et al. 2010, Science 330, 463 (LCROSS: 5.6 ± 2.9 wt% water ice in Cabeus); Li et al. 2018, PNAS 115, 8907 (M3: surface-exposed ice in polar cold traps)
ice.note: Region-level: ice is in cold traps (Cabeus is ~100 km away), not on the sunlit ridge surface itself.
